narration: This is KubeSage, an AI SRE team for Kubernetes. Here is how it works, in under three minutes.

First, the summary. KubeSage finds capacity you pay for but never use, and right-sizes it within guardrails. When something breaks, a team of AI agents gathers evidence, finds the cause, and writes the fix. Agent fixes become git commits that a person reviews before applying.

Picture a hypothetical online store on Azure Kubernetes. Five services share one general-purpose node at two hundred eighty dollars a month. Some requests were set high, just in case: two services reserve two cores each and use almost none. A cheaper compute-optimised node stands ready. Tonight, a ledger cache ships with too little memory.

To find waste, KubeSage reads thirty days of usage. Statistics are free, and healthy workloads stop after a quick triage. Only harder cases get more model reasoning. Guardrails floor requests from history and keep scaling within bounds. The result is a plan for requests, autoscaling, and the node pool.

When an alert fires, four small agents gather evidence in parallel: metrics, system resources, alerts, and security. A larger Thinker model reads their findings and your team's plain English rules to find the root cause. An Executor writes the fix. Policy checks limit each edit's scope and type, before the commit.
Here is the KubeSage dashboard on that simulated cluster. Each glass box is a pod, as tall as the CPU it reserves, filled as far as it is used.
Analyze finds that a cheaper node would save about thirty-four dollars a month, twelve percent. The model calls to find it cost about one cent.
Apply moves the right-sized services to the cheaper node. Report-worker scales to zero outside its nightly window.
Now the bad release ships. Ledger-cache needs more memory than its limit, so it is killed. The ContainerOOMKilled alert fires.
The team starts on its own. The four sub-agents report, the Thinker finds the cause, and the Executor writes the fix. The chat on the left shows each hand-off.
The commit raises ledger-cache's memory, proposes a memory-optimised node pool, and adds two security fixes. Sixteen seconds, two cents. A person decides what ships.
That is KubeSage. It finds the waste, fixes what breaks, and leaves the decision to a person.
